mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or equivalent corporate registry in the beneficial owner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing jurisdiction is party to the Hague Apostille Convention: notary certification of the certificate, then Apostille from that jurisdiction's Competent Authority. If the issuing jurisdiction is not a Hague member: notary certification, then authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then Consular legalization by the New Zealand embassy or consulate with consular jurisdiction. The two routes are parallel alternatives and must never be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All natural persons holding 25% or more of shares, voting rights, or ultimate control, plus proposed directors and secretaries, must be screened prior to incorporation and at least monthly thereafter against: (i) the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit Watchlist; (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Sanctions lists; (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions Lists; (iv) EU/UK consolidated financial sanctions lists; (v) NZ Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade autonomous sanctions notices; and (vi) adverse media and global enforcement databases. Ultimate beneficial owners who are politically exposed persons (PEPs), including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and close associates/family members, require senior-management approval and enhanced continuous monitoring of source of wealth, source of funds, and transaction purpose. Negative screening hits trigger an immediate and mandatory suspicious transaction report to NZFIU within three working days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Company Name Search and Name Reservation (MBIE Companies Register)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin script. Māori and transliterated English names are accepted, but names are not registered in Chinese characters. The name must comply with the four-tier convention: (1) unique distinctive element, (2) descriptive industry element, (3) restricted-word element requiring consent, and (4) mandatory legal suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. The name must not be the same or nearly the same as an existing company, reserved name, NZBN record, or registered trade mark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No extension of a name reservation is available. If the Registrar rejects a name, the applicant should first request written reasons, then file a reconsideration request with the New Zealand Companies Office within 15 working days, attaching the proposed name, alternative distinctive elements, a NZBN/trade-mark search, and consents from the relevant ministry for restricted words. If the Registrar maintains refusal, the applicant may file for judicial review in the High Court or submit a new reservation with a different distinctive name. IRD clearance and shareholder consent must accompany every resubmission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual street address is accepted by the Companies Office only if a physical registered office and a licensed agent are maintained; however, Inland Revenue and NZ banks will reject a pure virtual mailbox for GST/income-tax registration and account opening in the medical-device/OEM sector because the AML/CFT Act requires genuine commercial substance. For ISIC 3250/NAICS 334517, a virtual office without production facilities, staff, or local radiation-safety licensure is operationally inadequate and carries a high risk of de-risking.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) physical premises with signage; (2) lease or ownership deed; (3) production/inventory records; (4) payroll and employment records; (5) Radiation Safety Act licence/Medsafe conformity-assessment evidence; and (6) on-site board minutes. Quantified risk: approximately 15-20% for a newly incorporated manufacturing company within the first 24 months if GST-refund anomalies or related-party transactions are flagged; the unannounced inspection probability rises to 40% if a virtual-office registered address is used.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No. 102), especially sections 12-16 (incorporation and registered office), section 22 (name restrictions), section 37 and Part 5 (share allotment), sections 151-152 (director appointment and consent), section 24 (written resolutions), Part 11 (financial reporting), together with the New Zealand Business Number Act 2016 and the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 for any public offer of securities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the Companies Register and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZCN1 - Application for Incorporation of a Company (electronic lodgement through the Companies Office online portal, Companies Register, incorporating the reservation of company name, registered office particulars, director and shareholder details, and the constitution where adopted).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The Companies Act 1993 requires only that at least one share be issued at incorporation; shares may have no par value and may be issued for cash, unpaid capital, or non-monetary consideration at the discretion of the board. No escrow account or statutory deposit is required by the Registrar of Companies; directors must satisfy the solvency test under section 4 and the duty in section 135 of the Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [Company Name] LIMITED, PASSED UNANIMOUSLY IN WRITING ON [Date] IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CONSTITUTION OF THE COMPANY. RESOLVED THAT: 1. The allotment of the 100 subscriber ordinary shares (or such number as is stated in the incorporation application) to the subscribers named in the share register be and is hereby confirmed, ratified and recorded in the share register in accordance with the allotment provisions of Part 5 of the Companies Act 1993. 2. The registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [street address], New Zealand, an address physically open to the public at all reasonable times, and the Registrar of Companies and the Inland Revenue Department be notified pursuant to sections 16 and 17 of the Act. 3. The following directors, each having consented in accordance with section 152 of the Act, be and are hereby appointed to hold office until the first annual meeting: [Name] (Managing Director), [Name] (Finance Director), [Name] (Technical Director). 4. The Chief Executive Officer and Company Secretary (if any) be and are hereby authorised to open banking accounts, execute leases, register with the Inland Revenue, Medsafe, WorkSafe and the local council, and arrange external payment rails, being SWIFT letters of credit and telegraphic transfers, for the company's wholesale radiation-detector trade. 5. The first financial year of the Company shall close on the next 31 March, and the board may exercise the exemption from audit permitted under Part 11 of the Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Clearance and NZBN Preliminary Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register online name search facility (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the Companies Register. The proposed name must include 'Limited' or 'Ltd' and comply with section 22 of the Companies Act 1993: it must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, must not be objectionable or offensive, and must not contain restricted words (e.g., 'Bank', 'Trust', 'University') without the appropriate regulator consent. Save or print the search result as evidence for the incorporation application. The name is provisionally reserved upon successful search and will be formally reserved when the online incorporation application is submitted.
required_dossiers: Companies Register name search result summary
Statement of restricted-word consent from the relevant regulator (if any restricted term is used)
Director and shareholder identification details (passport, utility bill) for the application record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is objected to or refused, file a written submission to the Registrar under section 23 of the Act within 20 working days providing reasons why the name is not confusingly similar, or amend the name by adding a distinctive element (e.g., geographic or trade descriptor) and re-apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Adoption of the Company Constitution and Governance Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External NZ-qualified corporate legal counsel, to be authenticated and submitted with the incorporation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Decide whether to adopt the default constitution set out in Schedule 1 of the Companies Act 1993 or a bespoke constitution. If a bespoke constitution is to be adopted, it must be dated, executed, and contain provisions regarding share classes, director powers, pre-emptive rights, financial year end, board meeting quorum, and officer authority. The constitution must be lodged as part of the incorporation application if the board wishes it to have effect from registration. Where no constitution is lodged, the standard statutory default provisions apply automatically.
required_dossiers: Final executed constitution (if adopted)
Written resolution of the founding shareholders adopting the constitution
Legal opinion regarding consistency with sections 28-32 of the Companies Act 1993
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar or a third-party institution (e.g., bank) rejects the constitution for substantive defect, convene a special shareholders' meeting to amend it by special resolution in accordance with section 32 of the Act and re-file the amended version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Online Filing of the Incorporation Application (Form NZCN1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register online portal (Incorporation Application)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online incorporation application on the Companies Office website. Enter the company name, registered office physical address (must be a physical address in New Zealand and not a post office box), the constitution if adopted, the number of shares to be issued and the allocation among subscribers, and the full legal names, residential addresses, and consent details of each director and shareholder. Complete the director consent declaration required by section 152 of the Act. Electronically sign on behalf of each applicant, review the declaration of solvency, and pay the filing fee by credit card or bank transfer.
required_dossiers: Form NZCN1 (online fields)
Signed constitution (if any)
Director consent forms (declaration under section 152)
Subscriber information and share allocation schedule
Proof of payment of the NZ$105.71 (incl. GST) filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a notice of deficiency or query, correct the specified fields (e.g., registered office address, director disqualification declaration, or name availability) and resubmit within 20 working days. If further time is required, apply to the Registrar for an extension; if the name is invalid, resubmit with a substituted compliant name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / New Zealand Business Number Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon statutory approval, the Companies Office will issue the electronic Certificate of Incorporation recording the company name, registration number, and registration date, and will simultaneously allocate a unique 13-digit New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) under the NZBN Act 2016. Verify that all particulars on the certificate are accurate, then download the official PDF certificate and the company register extract from the Companies Register. These documents constitute the formal proof of legal existence.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (PDF issued by Companies Office)
Company details extract from the Companies Register
NZBN confirmation notice from MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error in company name or date, file a 'Notice of Change' or a formal request for correction with the Registrar supported by a statutory declaration. If the certificate is not auto-generated within the service level, contact the Companies Office service centre with the application reference to expedite issue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board of Directors Meeting - Adoption of Governance, Allotment and Banking Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company convened at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting in accordance with the statutory default provisions or the constitution. Pass the pro forma first board resolution covering: allotment and recording of subscriber shares; fixing the registered office (section 16); appointment of the Managing Director, Finance Director, Technical Director and Company Secretary (if appointed); approval of bank account opening and signatory powers; authorisation to execute lease and supply agreements; adoption of the financial year end; and approval of SWIFT LC/TT payment rails for the X-ray detector wholesale trade. Record the meeting in a minutes book maintained at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Pro forma first board resolution (minutes) signed by all directors
Directors' consents to act (section 152)
Notice of registered office and director details filed online with the Companies Office
Conflict-of-interest declarations under section 140 (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the meeting is challenged for lack of quorum, convene an adjourned meeting on due written notice. If a director has a material personal interest, record the declaration under section 140 and approve the resolution without the interested director's vote, or obtain a shareholders' ordinary resolution ratifying the decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with Inland Revenue (IRD, GST, PAYE, RWT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRC) - myIR online services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the company's NZBN and Certificate of Incorporation, register online via myIR to obtain an Inland Revenue Department (IRD) number for the company. Complete the company income tax registration (Form IRD409), elect the balance date (31 March), and register for GST if taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZ$60,000 over twelve months (recommended given the export-oriented OEM business model). If employees will be engaged, register as an employer for PAYE; if interest or dividends will be paid, register for RWT. Provide CRS/FATCA self-certification for all beneficial owners. Retain the IRD number confirmation for bank account opening.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Form IRD409 and GST registration form (if applicable)
Shareholder and director tax residence declarations
CRS-FATCA self-certification forms
Projected turnover statement for GST threshold determination
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD classification is incorrect, amend the company type and tax codes through myIR. If GST registration is filed late, request waiver of late-registration penalties by demonstrating reasonable cause (section 183A of the Tax Administration Act 1994) through the 'Request for relief' pathway in myIR.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Account and Funding of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered New Zealand commercial bank (e.g., ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac) operating under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Certificate of Incorporation, company register extract, IRD confirmation, constitution (if adopted), first board resolution appointing signatories, and identity documents of all beneficial owners holding 25% or more of the shares, to the bank's corporate onboarding department. The bank will conduct customer due diligence under the AML/CFT Act and may request a business plan and proof of source of funds for the share subscription. Once the account is open, deposit the subscriber consideration (no statutory minimum is required, but operating funds should be deposited) and activate SWIFT and telegraphic transfer (TT) rails for expected letter-of-credit transactions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and current company extract
IRD number confirmation letter
First board resolution (account signatories)
Passport of each director, shareholder, and beneficial owner
Source-of-funds declaration for share capital deposit
Business plan and projected transaction volume for payment rail approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank defers or rejects the application due to AML/CFT concerns, provide a corporate structure chart identifying all beneficial owners and the economic rationale for the New Zealand entity, and clarify the ultimate source of wealth. If rejection persists, file a formal internal dispute with the bank's compliance team or seek an alternative banking facility and, where justified, escalate to the Banking Ombudsman Scheme.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: WorkSafe Registration and Occupational Health and Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: WorkSafe New Zealand (the Government health and safety regulator)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company and the manufacturing facility as a Person Conducting a Business or Undertaking (PCBU) under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (HSW Act). Prepare a documented health and safety management system for the vacuum deposition facility covering hazard identification, chemical safety for cesium iodide and amorphous silicon precursors, confined-space entry, electrical work, and emergency preparedness. Appoint a health and safety officer, conduct worker induction, and, if operating with hazardous substances above trigger quantities, apply for a hazardous substances compliance certificate under the Health and Safety at Work (Hazardous Substances) Regulations 2017.
required_dossiers: WorkSafe PCBU registration confirmation
Hazardous substances inventory and safety data sheets (SDS) register
Health and safety policy and risk assessment under section 36 of the HSW Act 2015
Emergency response plan, fire and evacuation procedures
Proof of competency certificates for electrical and vacuum technology personnel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If WorkSafe issues an improvement or prohibition notice, prepare a corrective action plan within the stated deadline, engage a competent OHS consultant, and apply for internal review of the notice under section 164 of the HSW Act 2015. If a hazardous substances licence application is refused, amend the inventory to reduce trigger quantities or submit an appeal against the decision to the District Court within 28 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Medsafe Medical Device Manufacturing Notification and ISO 13485 Quality Management Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Medsafe (New Zealand Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority, Ministry of Health) together with a JAS-ANZ accredited third-party certifying body
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the company manufactures digital X-ray flat panel detectors (Class IIa/IIb medical devices under the Medicines (Medical Devices) Regulations 2022), the facility must complete a Medsafe Medical Device Notification (device inclusion in the ARTG-aligned NZ register) and operate a certified ISO 13485:2016 quality management system. Register the manufacturing site with a JAS-ANZ accredited registrar and obtain a GMP/quality system certificate covering the fabrication of amorphous silicon and cesium iodide detectors. Maintain a technical file demonstrating conformity with the applicable safety and performance standards, including IEC 60601-1 electrical safety and IEC 62304 software lifecycle standards where relevant.
required_dossiers: Medsafe Medical Device Notification form (Class IIa/IIb classification)
ISO 13485:2016 certificate issued by an accredited certifying body
Technical file or Design Dossier including clinical evaluation and risk management report (ISO 14971)
IEC 60601-1 type-test reports from an accredited test laboratory
Labelling and UDI-DI compliance statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Medsafe requests additional information (e.g., biocompatibility or EMC test data), file the supplementary test reports through the notification portal within the prescribed deadline. If the ISO 13485 certification is withheld by the registrar, implement corrective actions identified in the pre-assessment audit and request a re-audit; if Medsafe issues a non-compliant notification, appeal to the Director-General of Health under the Medicines Act 1981 and provide a corrective and preventive action (CAPA) plan.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Impact Assessment, Discharge Consents and Hazardous Substances Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand (for hazardous substances) and the relevant Regional Council / Territorial Authority (for resource consents and trade waste discharges)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary environmental impact assessment (EIA) screening for the vapor deposition plant. The proposed use of sealed vacuum chambers with cesium iodide and amorphous silicon is generally classified as a Permitted Activity under the relevant regional plan, subject to the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality 2004 and the National Environmental Standards for Water 2020. Apply for a Trade Waste Consent from the local council if process wastewater will be discharged to the municipal sewer; provide waste characterisation and effluent monitoring data demonstrating compliance with trace-metal limits. If hazardous substances (e.g., caustic etchants or high-purity solvent mixtures) exceed trigger quantities, submit a Hazardous Substances Notification and Location Licence application via EPA's HS-Notify service.
required_dossiers: EIA screening report prepared by a certified planner
Trade waste consent application with discharge characterisation data
EPA hazardous substances notification and location licence application
Air discharge permit application (if VOC or halide emissions exceed permitted thresholds)
Waste management and environmental monitoring plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Regional Council declines a discharge consent, lodge an appeal with the Environment Court under sections 120-121 of the Resource Management Act 1991 within 15 working days. If the discharge is non-compliant, redesign the process to implement a closed-loop zero-discharge scrubber and apply for a reclassification of the activity as a Permitted Activity. If the EPA refuses the hazardous substances location licence, reduce stored quantities below the trigger threshold and re-present the application with modified inventory data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire Safety Certification, Building Compliance and Building Warrant of Fitness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) and the local Territorial Authority (Building Consent Authority)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the industrial manufacturing premises, obtain a building consent and Code Compliance Certificate (CCC) from the Territorial Authority under the Building Act 2004. Arrange for a fire safety inspection by Fire and Emergency New Zealand covering means of escape, fire suppression systems, extinguishants, and hazardous goods storage. Prepare a compliance schedule for all fire protection and life safety systems and obtain an annual Building Warrant of Fitness (BWoF). Commission a structural load inspection of the cleanroom floor, mezzanine, and vacuum-chamber support plinths certified by a Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng).
required_dossiers: Building consent and Code Compliance Certificate (CCC)
Compliance schedule and Building Warrant of Fitness (BWoF)
FENZ fire safety inspection report and evacuation plan
Electrical safety certificate (ESC) from a licensed electrician
CPEng structural load inspection report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire safety inspection identifies non-compliance, carry out remedial works and submit a re-inspection request to FENZ within 20 working days. If the BWoF is issued with warnings, rectify the compliance schedule and obtain a further inspection from an Independent Qualified Person (IQP). If the building warrant is refused, appeal to the local authority in writing and, if necessary, to the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Medsafe (New Zealand Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority) for medical device manufacturing notification; WorkSafe New Zealand for occupational health and safety and hazardous substances compliance; and the relevant Regional Council / Territorial Authority for building, fire, and environmental permitting
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing Facility Notification (Medsafe) together with Hazardous Substances Location Licence (EPA HS-Notify), Trade Waste Consent (Regional Council), and Building Warrant of Fitness / Fire Safety Clearance (Building Act 2004 and FENZ procedures)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, jointly with the relevant Regional Council acting as the discharge consent authority under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 - Screening-level registration (Permitted Activity with standing discharge conditions under the regional plan and National Environmental Standards). No full EIA Report is mandated for medical device fabrication in a sealed vacuum-deposition process; a full EIA is triggered only if annual hazardous substances throughput exceeds the regional trigger volumes or if effluent discharge to natural water is proposed outside the sewer network.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Air Quality) 2004: daily PM10 limit 50 µg/m3; no offensive or objectionable odours beyond boundary; solvent-VOC abatement efficiency of at least 95% where solvent-containing deposition processes are used. Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Water) 2020: applies to point-source discharges; no detectable cesium or iodide in natural waters; halide concentration in wastewater not exceeding 0.1 mg/L; municipal Trade Waste limits for heavy metals (copper, lead, zinc) and pH 6.5-10.0 as set by the relevant council bylaw; hazardous waste (cesium iodide residues, spent cathode targets) must be classified, labelled and removed by an authorised carrier to a permitted disposal facility with full job site manifests retained for five years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from Fire and Emergency New Zealand covering means of escape, suppression systems, emergency lighting, and hazardous goods storage; Building Warrant of Fitness and compliance schedule under the Building Act 2004; structural load inspection and cleanroom certification by a Chartered Professional Engineer; WorkSafe occupational clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 including electrical safety, hazardous substance storage, and safe work method statements; annual testing of hydrants, extinguishers, and fire alarm systems; and approval of the Chemical Inventory and Emergency Response Plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake); online portal 'myIR' at https://www.ird.govt.nz; corporate registry and NZBN issuance via the New Zealand Companies Office at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident foreign entity establishing a New Zealand presence or a NZ-incorporated subsidiary: (1) Incorporate the company with the New Zealand Companies Office to obtain an NZBN and company number, or register the overseas company as a branch; (2) Apply for an IRD number via myIR online or by submitting form IR596/IR742 (non-resident company), and register for GST on the same application or via the GSTR form; (3) If hiring staff, register for PAYE employer obligations; (4) For physical export/import operations, obtain an importer/exporter client code from the New Zealand Customs Service through the Trade Single Window; (5) A non-resident company without a New Zealand fixed establishment may separately register for GST using the 'non-resident remote services' registration process, generally through a nominated New Zealand tax agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (New Zealand resident companies are taxed at the flat corporate rate of 28% on worldwide income; non-resident companies are taxed only on New Zealand-source income attributable to a permanent establishment. Closely held qualifying companies may elect look-through company pass-through treatment.)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Look-Through Company (LTC) election: a New Zealand close company (five or fewer natural-person shareholders, no corporate shareholder) may elect to be tax-transparent, flowing income, losses, and credits through to shareholders. Portfolio Investment Entity (PIE) election: qualifying investment vehicles may elect a flat 28% entity-level tax. No general 'check-the-box' regime exists; however, the hybrid mismatch rules (Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018) automatically recharacterise cross-border payments involving hybrid entities/branches, including NZ branch elections that create hybrid mismatches, and deny deductions or impose countermeasures without elective relief.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) – a value-added tax administered under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 – compulsory registration applies to any supplier whose taxable supplies in New Zealand exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period (or is reasonably expected to exceed that amount in the next 12 months). The same NZD 60,000 threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of remote services (cross-border B2C digital services and remote services), who may also voluntarily register.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government pre-approval of invoices exists. Electronic invoicing is voluntary, with a national Peppol framework facilitating B2B and B2G e-invoicing interoperability. GST returns must be filed electronically via the Inland Revenue 'myIR' portal (or through approved intermediaries/software) on a monthly or two-monthly basis, and payments settled by the due date. Physical export declarations are filed electronically through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window, not via a fiscal invoice stamping mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, exports of goods are zero-rated if: (i) the supplier exports the goods themselves, or on the supplier's behalf, within 28 days of the time of supply (within 12 months for goods supplied under hire purchase or conditional sale); (ii) the goods are supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply and the goods are subsequently exported before being used in New Zealand; or (iii) the goods are supplied for removal to an offshore installation or on a 'call-off' basis. Under section 11A, services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, provided the services are not supplied in connection with New Zealand land or physical goods in New Zealand, and are not supplied to a resident for use in New Zealand. Digital X-ray flat panel detector OEM supplies (goods manufactured in NZ and shipped to foreign medical device distributors) qualify for zero-rating if the 28-day export rule is met and documentary evidence is retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service Export Declaration (filed electronically via the Trade Single Window under the Customs and Excise Act 2018)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of the goods
Commercial Invoice and Packing List (showing overseas buyer, HS/ISIC classification, quantity, and value)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by the New Zealand settlement bank confirming receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Certificate of Origin (where preferential tariff treatment under a free trade agreement is claimed)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Commissioner of Inland Revenue may reassess within 4 years (extended to 8 years for evasion) to claw back improperly zero-rated GST, recovering the 15% GST shortfall plus Use of Money Interest (UOMI) from the date the tax was originally due. Shortfall penalties under Part 9 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply strictly: 20% for lack of reasonable care; 20% for an unacceptable tax position (where a significant position lacks a reasonable basis); 40% for gross carelessness; 100% for an abusive tax position (dominant purpose of tax avoidance); and 150% for evasion or an equivalent act. Criminal prosecution under sections 143A–143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994 is available for knowingly providing false documentation or evading GST, with fines up to NZD 50,000 for the first offence and NZD 100,000 for subsequent offences, and imprisonment of up to 5 years for evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) acting as the central bank and prudential regulator; the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) supervises conduct and financial services licensing. Foreign exchange administration is liberalised, with no separate exchange-control authority or State Administration-style FX licensing requirement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully convertible on both current and capital account. There are no exchange-control laws, no surrender requirements, and no restrictions on the repatriation of branch profits, dividends, or liquidation proceeds. Profit remittance is subject only to standard tax compliance, notably non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) at 15% (subject to treaty reduction, e.g., 5% under the New Zealand–China double tax agreement where applicable), and to banking due diligence under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT). For a non-resident-owned NZ Limited manufacturing digital X-ray flat panel detectors, capital injections and trade settlements may flow freely in NZD and foreign currency accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies. Exporters are free to retain proceeds in foreign currency accounts (Foreign Currency Accounts or FCAs) without any Reserve Bank mandate to convert into NZD. Receipts may be held offshore or repatriated at the entity's discretion. The only obligations are documentary record-keeping for tax, AML/CFT source-of-funds verification, and, where export payments are routed through the New Zealand banking system, standard SWIFT/TT purpose-coding requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (NZD Settlement) and Foreign Currency Account (USD/EUR)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for operational acceleration. Licensed digital financial service providers registered on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR), such as Airwallex (NZ) Limited and Wise NZ Limited, are viable for low-value trade disbursements, cross-border collections, and multi-currency wallets. However, they are not licensed as registered banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021 and cannot provide NZD settlement account guarantees or letter-of-credit issuance. For a medical device OEM undertaking SWIFT LC and TT wire payments, the prescribed clearing rail remains a tier-1 locally incorporated bank; EMIs are legally constrained from operating unrestricted commercial credit products and must hold client funds in segregated trust accounts with an NZ prudentially regulated bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A hybrid mandate applies. Fully remote onboarding is generally unavailable for non-resident-owned manufacturing entities; at least one director or authorised senior officer must either attend an in-branch identity verification interview, or complete an interactive remote video call with a dedicated relationship manager and corporate compliance officer. In practice, tier-1 NZ banks require a physical New Zealand registered office and frequently request a face-to-face meeting for foreign UBOs. The banking compliance officer may accept a certified-jurisdiction notarisation package where the director cannot travel, but the bank retains discretion. For entities in the Low_Risk_Standard AML tier (medical devices OEM), a documented remote interview is typically acceptable provided an NZ resident director is appointed and source-of-funds evidence is produced.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) controlling the NZ subsidiary from a jurisdiction without comprehensive AML/CFT supervisory equivalence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport and national identity documents of each UBO; recent utility bill or bank statement proving residential address; UBO declaration and corporate structure chart; tax identification number and foreign tax residency certificate; FATF-aligned financial institution reference letter from the UBO's home bank; independent sanctions and adverse-media screening report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound equity capital injection for the NZ startup with opaque source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements or tax returns of the investing shareholder for the last two years; sale-and-purchase agreement, dividend declaration, or trust deed evidencing accumulated wealth; signed sworn affidavit of source of funds; bank statements showing the originating account and transaction trail; board resolution approving the capital injection and share allotment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade settlement profile involving high-value OEM shipments of digital X-ray detectors to hospitals and distributors in Asia-Pacific
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed OEM supply agreements and distributor contracts; proforma invoices and final commercial invoices; packing lists, bills of lading/air waybills, and customs entry evidence; statutory medical device registration or conformity marking (e.g., Medsafe approval path, ISO 13485 certificate, CE/FDA where applicable); declaration of anticipated transaction volumes and counterparty detail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No substantive New Zealand physical presence or local resident director on appointments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Confirmation of appointment of a New Zealand resident director and corporate secretary; registered office address and lease agreement; evidence of planned local operations (manufacturing facility lease, warehouse agreement, or local distributor arrangement); board minutes authorising banking signatories; Company Office (NZ Companies Register) certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital from the non-resident shareholder is routed via SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) to the NZ subsidiary's NZD or USD account at a tier-1 New Zealand bank, citing OECD Balance of Payments purpose code 'ED51 – Direct investment: equity capital' or the bank-specific inward remittance purpose code for equity participation. The remitter must reference the share subscription agreement and the NZ company's IRD number in the payment narrative. Verification procedures comprise source-of-funds documentary checks, anti-money-laundering screening, and confirmation that the transaction does not trigger Overseas Investment Act 2005 screening (share subscription in a medical device manufacturing entity is not a sensitive sector, nor does it involve sensitive land or significant business assets, so no OIA consent is required). The funds are then recorded in the company's equity ledger and the share allotment is filed with the New Zealand Companies Office.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for component procurement and logistics settlement are executed primarily via SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for open-account suppliers, and via irrevocable commercial letters of credit (documentary credits governed by UCP 600) for high-value and first-time counterparties. The NZD clearing leg utilises the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESSA) operated by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand through settlement bank participants. USD and other foreign-currency payments are settled through the bank's nostro accounts and correspondent banking network. Supporting documentation for each disbursement includes the underlying purchase order, supplier invoice, customs declaration, and where applicable, presentation documents conforming to the LC terms (commercial invoice, bill of lading, insurance certificate, and certificate of origin).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: NZD/USD outright deliverable FX forwards (tenors up to 12 months) transacted under an ISDA or bank master agreement
NZD/USD FX swaps for rolling near-dated liquidity and settlement timing mismatches
Cross-currency swaps to convert USD-denominated trade liabilities into NZD on a cost-effective fixed/floating basis
Vanilla FX options (buy-side protection only) – permits hedging of adverse NZD/USD moves while preserving upside on favourable exchange rate movements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Register corporate renewal filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) — Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within the month of the company's Annual Return Date, which is the first day of the month following the incorporation anniversary; the return must be filed on or before the last day of that month (e.g., incorporated 10 March → Annual Return Date 1 April → due 30 April each year).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic late filing penalty of NZD 200 per overdue return; after approximately 2 months of non-compliance the Registrar issues a Notice of Intention to Remove the company; failure to remedy within the statutory notice period leads to strike-off from the New Zealand Companies Register and dissolution of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements (General Purpose Financial Statements) and Auditor's Report, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (filed through the Companies Register); prepared and audited under External Reporting Board (XRB) standards
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 20 working days after the financial statements are delivered to shareholders; the annual report must be delivered within 5 months of balance date for a 31 March balance date (deliver by 31 August, file by late September); mandatory only for large companies or where shareholders holding 5%+ have requisitioned an audit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; company and each director are liable to fines of up to NZD 10,000; persistent non-filing permits the Companies Office to initiate removal and deregistration proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (IR4) and Provisional Tax Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July (paper) or 23 July (electronic); companies retaining a tax agent may be extended to 31 March of the following year; provisional tax is payable in three instalments during the income year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: initial penalty of NZD 250 plus NZD 50 per month up to NZD 1,000; late payment: initial penalty of 1% of the unpaid tax, further penalties of 1% per month thereafter, and use-of-money interest; IRD may issue a statutory demand and initiate formal debt collection or company liquidation proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is required for a New Zealand company that qualifies as 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, i.e., meets at least two of the following thresholds in each of the two preceding accounting periods: total assets exceeding NZD 60 million, total revenue exceeding NZD 30 million, or 50 or more full-time equivalent employees. Mandatory audit also applies where shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares requisition an audit, where the company's constitution requires it, or where the company is an FMC reporting entity. All other private companies are exempt unless a shareholder or creditor triggers the audit right.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ IFRS (New Zealand equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards) for Tier 1 entities; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR) for Tier 2 entities; NZ Simple Format Reporting (NZSFR – Accrual and Cash) for Tier 3 and Tier 4 small entities; all applied under the Companies Act 1993, Financial Reporting Act 2013, and XRB Accounting Standards Framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a separate annual UBO declaration form for private companies; beneficial ownership is evidenced through the Register of Members, which must be updated within 10 working days of any share transfer. The Annual Return filed with the Companies Register confirms the current registered shareholders and director details. Where the company acts as an AML/CFT reporting entity or designated non-financial business, customer due diligence and beneficial-owner records must be verified and retained under the AML/CFT Act 2009; otherwise, the board should annually review the share register and any chain of ownership to ensure persons holding directly or indirectly 25% or more of the shares are accurately recorded.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (general meetings and directors' resolutions)
Share Transfer Register (notations within the Register of Members)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 – 1,200 per annum for a serviced registered office and corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – 18,000 per annum for a mid-sized medical-device OEM manufacturing entity; small companies below the large threshold are generally exempt and incur USD 0 unless a shareholder requisitions an audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_rule: Losses carried forward indefinitely under s IA 4 ITA 2007 subject to 49% shareholder continuity (s IA 5) or business continuity test
